reproduction.scope: Reviewed current code and isolated synthetic Storage; no network, archived code or actual source/consumer reads

before_tests.scope: Current source and synthetic storage only; archived source not executed

improvements: One strict parser rejects duplicate decoded keys at every depth, JSON nonfinite constants and floating-point overflow while preserving ordinary finite numeric types, explicit zero, false, null and literal text.

Native capture, upstream proof parsing, retained inputs/output/manifest replay, current predecessor/readback and existing request-state reads share strict parsing. Both current HTTP handlers return a controlled unavailable response for ambiguous or non-object JSON.

Source bytes are retained before interpretation. Bounded upstream proof bytes are retained before validation. Malformed source packets are withheld and their exact retained replay reproduces that exclusion. A parseable source cannot claim malformed status.

Upstream proof/capture failures do not attempt publication. A failed publication-stage readback reports publication_status=unverified rather than claiming rollback; it does not overwrite a possible concurrent winner.
limitations: Exact native and static deployment acceptance remain pending.
Normal scheduled publication is separate and unverified.
This establishes parser integrity, not upstream economic correctness, original historical availability, model qualification or allocation authority.
The browser has a separately reproduced duplicate-key acceptance gap and is next work.
Dynamic current-writer source binding remains unproven. A publication-stage failure does not certify rollback or absence of a write.
